That comes from one line in OpenAI’s new Businesses in ChatGPT policy. A profile may also include information from other sources, and OpenAI says it doesn’t verify every detail or resolve every factual dispute, which leaves accuracy with you.

In this clip from Manual Focus, Hannah and I land on a plain recommendation. Claim the profile this month, give it one named owner, and treat the mention count as a signal until OpenAI says what it counts.

clips.text: Let's talk about the profile itself. Why does claiming it matter if I can't see the conversations? Because of one line in the policy. It says a profile may also include information from other sources. So ChatGPT can describe your business whether you claim it or not. And the policy says OpenAI doesn't verify every detail or resolve every factual dispute, so getting it right is your job. That sounds like a Google Business Profile with a different logo. Close enough, and it should sit with the same person. Only the owner or someone authorised can manage it, and misleading claims about prices or availability are banned. Our view, then, is to claim it this month and give it one named owner, and treat the mention count as a signal rather than a target until OpenAI says what it counts.

Hand AI your ChatGPT profile details and your site's key pages, and you get back a table of mismatches.

OpenAI's Business Hub lets a business claim its profile in ChatGPT and see mentions and website clicks. This clip from Manual Focus covers two jobs I would hand to AI once you have claimed yours.

The first is the audit. Give it your Business Hub profile details, your product feed and your site's contact, hours and pricing pages, and it returns every mismatch with the correct value.

The second is a weekly baseline. Give it the Business Hub figures, the AI referral sessions from your analytics and Bing's AI report. It gives you one trend table and flags when Hub clicks and real sessions drift apart.

The podcast voices are AI-generated.

The full episode, article and prompts are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/businesses-in-chatgpt-business-hub-brands/
clips.text: So what do you hand over? Get AI on this, first job. Audit what the profile says against your own site. Give it the details from your Business Hub profile and your product feed, plus your site's contact, hours and pricing pages. It hands back a table of every mismatch, from wrong opening hours to a price that's out of date, with the correct value and where it found it. Second job. Turn the numbers into a weekly baseline. Set it as a weekly routine. Each week, give it the Business Hub figures, the AI referral sessions from your analytics and Bing's AI report, and it gives you one trend table. It should also flag when Hub clicks and real sessions drift apart.
